messages:
mina: Quick heads-up1: proposing microsegmentation + RBAC tighten for the on-prem keystore in priv-deploy. Goal: eliminate cluster-scoped binding, keep all keystore activity namespace-isolated, and ensure forensic linkage for KMS/HSM ops.

vasu: Sounds good. Minimal roles?

mina: Role `keystore-reader` (get,list,watch secrets/pods), Role `keystore-rotator` (update secrets/keystore-certs only), Role `keystore-audit` (create events + create auditlogs.myorg.io). Bind to SA `keystore-agent`. No ClusterRole.

kevin: Network-wise: deny ingress to keystore ns; egress allowlist only to HSM CIDRs on TCP 1696, plus DNS (53) and NTP (123). No control-plane egress.

sec-bot: [automated] Dry-run hint: `kubectl auth reconcile --manifest=keystore-roles.yaml --dry-run=server`

mina: For correlation we will inject an e2e hashed-id: header `x-rw-eid` = sha256(namespace+request_id) on KMS calls and also stamp the apiserver audit webhook. This avoids exposing plaintext SA names in exported indexes.

vasu: Incident play if 403s: alert `KeystoreAuthFailure`; run `kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:keystore:keystore-agent get secrets/keystore-certs`; if denied revert RoleBinding, collect audit webhook entry and HSM trace using `x-rw-eid`. Open channel #priv-deploy-ops.

kevin: Vulnerability note: scanner found outdated libssl. Do NOT do RBAC+image bump in same rollout. RBAC & NetPol first, verify audit pairing, then image patch in separate canary.

mina: Adding a preflight smoke script to runbook (auth checks, netpol simulator, HSM ping) and ephemeral SRE access flow (OIDC 30m tokens, session recording). Will open PR with manifests + runbook and tag @vasu @kevin for review. :lock:
